quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials makes you more visible. Wear them all the time to stay safe.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. These signs show road rules that you must follow.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help reduce crash risk?

options.text: Watch for hazards and be ready to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, make sure other drivers see you. Signal your turns clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle. Watch the road ahead and be ready to react to dangers.

questions.question: Why might you drift into another lane while turning?

options.text: You are going too fast for the turn.
You do not know how to steer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are going too fast for the turn.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: What should you NOT do on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake quickly.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down gradually. Avoid quick movements. Use both brakes gently. Do not brake hard.

questions.question: How can you help a driver merge safely from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is their job to see you.
Move to a different lane away from the ramp if you can.
Weave back and forth in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the ramp if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space. If possible, change lanes away from the entrance ramp. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to make room.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jolt and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jolt and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jolt and a warning light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jolt and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, your motorcycle will jolt and the rear tire may skid. You could lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, how does it affect your motorcycle?

options.text: Faster to speed up, but slower to stop.
Slower to speed up and slower to stop.
Slower to speed up, but faster to stop.
Faster to speed up and faster to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower to speed up and slower to stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle slower to accelerate and slower to stop.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a crash?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Look only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance moves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance moves.
questions.explanation: Be visible to others. Signal your turns. Keep distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles. Watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Be ready to react quickly to unexpected hazards.

questions.question: What should a passenger do while you are riding?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with you during turns. They should sit as close to you as comfortable without crowding you. They should hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time for best control.

questions.question: When braking on slippery surfaces, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use gentle braking. This helps you keep control and avoid skidding.

questions.question: If one rider in your group wants to go faster, what should the group do?

options.text: Let that rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
Split up so each rider can go their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let that rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster, let them ride ahead safely. Plan to meet at a specific spot later.

questions.question: To be more visible to other drivers, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on all the time.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on all the time.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on day and night. Also wear bright and reflective clothes, and change your lane position to stay visible.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:
questions.correctAnswerText: Involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: Most crashes involve riders who are new to riding motorcycles.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and beside your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and beside your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane beside you. You may see the edge of your shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you avoid hazards on the road.
Give you a way to escape danger.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that keeps you safe. Your position should help you see and be seen, avoid hazards, stay out of blind spots, and escape danger. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: Where are motorcycles most likely to have conflicts with other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections have the most potential for conflicts. Be alert when other vehicles might cross your path.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn can:

options.text: Usually not be heard by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get someone's attention quickly.
questions.explanation: Your horn can get someone's attention fast. However, a motorcycle horn is quieter than a car horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Never rely only on your horn to handle a hazard.

questions.question: When another vehicle is tailgating you closely, you should:

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely and let them go ahead of you. Speeding up may only make it worse.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards and conditions.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Adjust both mirrors before you start your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and the lanes next to you.

questions.question: What should you do with a motorcycle helmet after a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Replaced.
questions.explanation: Replace your helmet if it has been in a crash. It cannot provide proper protection after impact.

questions.question: Your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
Tighten your hold on the handle grips and increase your speed to get past the hazard.
Ride on the shoulder instead of on the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is normal and not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.
